snapshots.name: Adam
snapshots.subtitle: The first man
snapshots.body: Adam is formed from the dust and placed in the garden of Eden, given the task of naming the animals and tending the ground. His disobedience over the forbidden fruit brings him and his descendants out from Eden into a life of labor.

snapshots.name: Eve
snapshots.subtitle: The first woman
snapshots.body: Eve is formed from Adam’s side to be his companion and is deceived by the serpent into eating the forbidden fruit, which she shares with Adam. She becomes, in the text’s own words, "the mother of all living."

snapshots.name: Cain
snapshots.subtitle: Firstborn of Adam and Eve
snapshots.body: Cain is a tiller of the ground whose offering God rejects in favor of his brother Abel’s; consumed by jealousy, he murders Abel in the field. Marked by God and driven out, he becomes a wanderer and founds a city.

snapshots.name: Abel
snapshots.subtitle: Second son of Adam and Eve
snapshots.body: Abel is a keeper of sheep whose offering of the firstlings of his flock God accepts. He is murdered by his brother Cain, becoming the first death in the biblical narrative.

snapshots.name: Noah
snapshots.subtitle: Builder of the ark
snapshots.body: Noah is the one righteous man of his generation, instructed by God to build an ark to save his family and pairs of every animal from a coming flood. After the waters recede he offers sacrifice and receives God’s covenant, marked by the rainbow.

snapshots.name: Abram
snapshots.subtitle: Called out of Ur
snapshots.body: Abram is called by God to leave his country for a land he will be shown, with the promise that he will become a great nation. He journeys through Canaan and Egypt with his wife Sarai and nephew Lot, his faith tested repeatedly along the way.

snapshots.name: Abraham
snapshots.subtitle: Father of many nations
snapshots.body: Renamed by God as the sign of an everlasting covenant, Abraham becomes the father of Isaac in his old age and, in the Bible’s starkest test of faith, is asked to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah before an angel stays his hand. He dies at a great age and is buried beside Sarah at Machpelah.

snapshots.name: Sarai
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Abram
snapshots.body: Sarai is Abram’s wife, barren into old age, who gives her servant Hagar to Abram so that he might have an heir through her instead.

snapshots.name: Sarah
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Abraham, mother of Isaac
snapshots.body: Renamed by God alongside her husband, Sarah laughs at the promise that she will bear a son in her old age, then names that son Isaac, meaning laughter, when he is born. She dies at Hebron and is the first person buried in the cave of Machpelah.

snapshots.name: Hagar
snapshots.subtitle: Egyptian servant of Sarah
snapshots.body: Hagar bears Abraham a son, Ishmael, and is twice driven into the wilderness, where an angel finds and comforts her. She becomes the mother of a great nation in her own right, through Ishmael.

snapshots.name: Ishmael
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Abraham and Hagar
snapshots.body: Ishmael is Abraham’s firstborn son, born of Hagar, sent away with his mother once Isaac is born but promised by God that he too will father a great nation. He grows up an archer in the wilderness of Paran.

snapshots.name: Isaac
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Abraham and Sarah
snapshots.body: Isaac is the long-promised son of Abraham’s old age, nearly offered as a sacrifice on Mount Moriah before God provides a ram instead. He marries Rebekah, and in his old age is deceived into giving his blessing to Jacob instead of Esau.

snapshots.name: Rebekah
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Isaac
snapshots.body: Rebekah is chosen at a well by Abraham’s servant to be Isaac’s wife, and later favors her younger son Jacob, helping him deceive the blind Isaac into giving him the blessing meant for Esau.

snapshots.name: Jacob
snapshots.subtitle: Younger son of Isaac and Rebekah
snapshots.body: Jacob buys his brother Esau’s birthright for a bowl of stew and later disguises himself to steal their father’s blessing, fleeing to his uncle Laban’s house. There he marries Leah and Rachel and grows wealthy in flocks before setting out for home.

snapshots.name: Israel
snapshots.subtitle: Father of the twelve tribes
snapshots.body: Renamed after wrestling all night with a divine stranger at Peniel, Jacob becomes Israel and is reconciled with Esau. His twelve sons by four women become the twelve tribes, and in his old age he is reunited with his son Joseph in Egypt.

snapshots.name: Esau
snapshots.subtitle: Elder son of Isaac and Rebekah, twin of Jacob
snapshots.body: Esau is a skillful hunter who sells his birthright to his brother Jacob for a meal and is later cheated of their father’s blessing as well. Years later he greets the returning Jacob with an embrace rather than the vengeance Jacob feared.

snapshots.name: Rachel
snapshots.subtitle: Younger wife of Jacob
snapshots.body: Rachel is Jacob’s beloved wife, for whom he labors fourteen years, and the long-barren mother of Joseph and Benjamin. She dies giving birth to Benjamin on the road to Bethlehem.

snapshots.name: Leah
snapshots.subtitle: Elder wife of Jacob
snapshots.body: Leah is given to Jacob in place of her sister Rachel through her father Laban’s deception, and bears him six sons including Judah and Levi, ancestors of the priestly and royal lines.

snapshots.name: Joseph
snapshots.subtitle: Favored son of Jacob
snapshots.body: Joseph, favored by his father and given a coat of many colors, is sold into slavery in Egypt by his jealous brothers. Through dream interpretation he rises to become Pharaoh’s chief minister and later saves his own family from famine, forgiving his brothers.

snapshots.name: Judah
snapshots.subtitle: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah
snapshots.body: Judah persuades his brothers to sell Joseph rather than kill him, and later offers himself as a slave in place of Benjamin, moving Joseph to reveal himself. His descendants become the royal tribe from which David and, in Christian reading, Jesus descend.

snapshots.name: Benjamin
snapshots.subtitle: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel
snapshots.body: Benjamin is Jacob’s youngest and most cherished son, born at the cost of his mother Rachel’s life. His brothers’ fear of losing him too becomes the turning point that leads Joseph to reveal himself to them in Egypt.

snapshots.name: Lot
snapshots.subtitle: Nephew of Abraham
snapshots.body: Lot travels with his uncle Abraham before settling near the wicked city of Sodom, from which he is rescued by angels just before its destruction. His wife looks back at the ruin and is turned to a pillar of salt.

snapshots.name: Melchizedek
snapshots.subtitle: Priest-king of Salem
snapshots.body: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blesses Abram and receives a tithe from him after a battle. Later writers use him as a type of an eternal priesthood outside the ordinary Levitical line.

snapshots.name: Moses
snapshots.subtitle: Deliverer and lawgiver
snapshots.body: Moses, drawn from the Nile as a baby and raised in Pharaoh’s household, flees to Midian after killing an Egyptian and is called by God from a burning bush to free the Israelites from slavery. He leads them through the parted sea, receives the law at Sinai, and guides them through forty years in the wilderness, though he himself dies before entering the promised land.

snapshots.name: Aaron
snapshots.subtitle: Brother of Moses, first high priest
snapshots.body: Aaron serves as Moses’s spokesman before Pharaoh and performs signs with his rod, but also casts the golden calf the people worship in Moses’s absence. He is later consecrated as Israel’s first high priest, a role that passes to his descendants.

snapshots.name: Miriam
snapshots.subtitle: Sister of Moses and Aaron
snapshots.body: Miriam watches over the infant Moses in the bulrushes and later leads the women of Israel in song after the crossing of the sea. She is struck with a skin disease after challenging Moses’s authority and dies in the wilderness at Kadesh.

snapshots.name: Pharaoh
snapshots.subtitle: King of Egypt at the exodus
snapshots.body: The Pharaoh of the exodus enslaves the Israelites and repeatedly refuses Moses’s demand to let them go, his heart hardening through ten devastating plagues. He pursues the departing Israelites to the Red Sea, where his army is destroyed.

snapshots.name: Joshua
snapshots.subtitle: Moses’s chosen fighter
snapshots.body: Joshua is the man Moses tells to choose men and go out to fight Amalek at Rephidim, while Moses stands on the hilltop with the rod of God in his hand.

snapshots.name: Joshua
snapshots.subtitle: Successor to Moses
snapshots.body: Joshua, one of the twelve spies sent into Canaan and one of only two who urged trust in God’s promise, succeeds Moses as leader of Israel. He leads the conquest of Canaan, beginning with the fall of Jericho, and divides the land among the tribes.

snapshots.name: Caleb
snapshots.subtitle: Spy of the tribe of Judah
snapshots.body: Caleb is the other of the twelve spies who, with Joshua, trusted God’s promise about Canaan against the fearful report of the majority. For his faith he is granted the hill country of Hebron as his inheritance in old age.

snapshots.name: Balaam
snapshots.subtitle: Hired prophet
snapshots.body: Balaam is a foreign prophet hired by King Balak to curse Israel, but is stopped on the road by an angel his donkey sees before he does. He ultimately can only bless Israel, though he later corrupts them by another scheme.

snapshots.name: Deborah
snapshots.subtitle: Judge and prophetess
snapshots.body: Deborah is a prophetess and judge who summons Barak to lead Israel’s army against the Canaanite general Sisera, and sings a victory song afterward. Her sure-footed leadership is contrasted with Barak’s hesitance.

snapshots.name: Gideon
snapshots.subtitle: Judge who defeats Midian
snapshots.body: Gideon, threshing wheat in hiding from Midianite raiders, is called by an angel to deliver Israel and tests God twice with a fleece before acting. With a force cut down to just three hundred men, he routs the Midianite camp by night with torches and trumpets.

snapshots.name: Samson
snapshots.subtitle: Nazirite strongman
snapshots.body: Samson, a judge of Israel set apart from birth and given great strength as long as his hair is uncut, wages a one-man war against the Philistines. Betrayed by Delilah, who learns the secret of his strength, he is blinded and enslaved before pulling down a temple on his captors in his final act.

snapshots.name: Delilah
snapshots.subtitle: Philistine woman who betrays Samson
snapshots.body: Delilah is bribed by the Philistine lords to discover the secret of Samson’s strength, and after repeated attempts wears him down until he tells her the truth about his hair. She has it cut while he sleeps, delivering him into his enemies’ hands.

snapshots.name: Ruth
snapshots.subtitle: Moabite widow
snapshots.body: Ruth, a Moabite widow, refuses to leave her mother-in-law Naomi and returns with her to Bethlehem, gleaning in the fields to support them both. Her loyalty leads to marriage with Boaz, and she becomes an ancestor of David.

snapshots.name: Naomi
snapshots.subtitle: Mother-in-law of Ruth
snapshots.body: Naomi, widowed and having lost both her sons in Moab, returns to Bethlehem bitter with grief, urging her daughters-in-law to remain behind. Ruth’s loyalty and the birth of a grandson restore her.

snapshots.name: Boaz
snapshots.subtitle: Kinsman-redeemer of Ruth
snapshots.body: Boaz, a wealthy relative of Naomi’s late husband, shows Ruth favor in his fields and, following custom, redeems her through marriage. Their son Obed becomes the grandfather of David.

snapshots.name: Samuel
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet and last judge
snapshots.body: Samuel, given to the LORD’s service by his mother Hannah before his birth, hears God’s voice as a boy in the temple at Shiloh and grows into Israel’s last judge and a prophet. He anoints first Saul and then David as king, and rebukes Saul when he disobeys God.

snapshots.name: Eli
snapshots.subtitle: Priest and judge at Shiloh
snapshots.body: Eli, the priest who raises the boy Samuel at the tabernacle in Shiloh, fails to restrain his own corrupt sons. He dies of shock on hearing that the ark of God has been captured in battle.

snapshots.name: Saul
snapshots.subtitle: First king of Israel
snapshots.body: Saul, a tall young Benjamite chosen and anointed as Israel’s first king, wins early victories but is rejected by God for repeated disobedience. Tormented by jealousy of David and an evil spirit, he ends his reign in defeat, taking his own life on Mount Gilboa.

snapshots.name: David
snapshots.subtitle: Descendant of Ruth and Boaz
snapshots.body: David is named at the end of the book of Ruth as the son of Jesse, whose line is traced back through Obed to Boaz and Ruth.

snapshots.name: David
snapshots.subtitle: Shepherd who becomes king
snapshots.body: David, the youngest son of Jesse anointed in secret by Samuel, kills the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and rises from court musician to fugitive to king. He unites Israel, captures Jerusalem, and is promised an everlasting dynasty, though his reign is marred by his affair with Bathsheba and family rebellion.

snapshots.name: Bathsheba
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Uriah, then of David
snapshots.body: Bathsheba is seen bathing by David, who sends for her and, on learning she is pregnant, arranges the death of her husband Uriah to cover the affair. The child of the affair dies, but she later bears Solomon and secures his succession to the throne.

snapshots.name: Uriah the Hittite
snapshots.subtitle: Bathsheba’s husband
snapshots.body: Uriah is a loyal soldier in David’s army whose refusal to visit his own house while his comrades are at war leads David to have him placed at the front of the fiercest fighting, where he is killed.

snapshots.name: Nathan
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet under David
snapshots.body: Nathan the prophet confronts David over Bathsheba and Uriah with a parable that exposes the king’s own guilt, and later ensures that Solomon rather than a rival son succeeds to the throne.

snapshots.name: Jonathan
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Saul, friend of David
snapshots.body: Jonathan, Saul’s son and heir, forms a deep friendship with David and repeatedly protects him from his father’s jealous rage, even though it costs him the throne. He dies alongside Saul in battle against the Philistines.

snapshots.name: Absalom
snapshots.subtitle: Son of David
snapshots.body: Absalom avenges his sister Tamar by killing their brother Amnon, then later leads an open rebellion against his father David. His revolt collapses and he dies caught by his hair in a tree, grieved deeply by David despite the betrayal.

snapshots.name: Joab
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Zeruiah
snapshots.body: Joab is named as the brother of Abishai and the son of Zeruiah, one of the men who follow David.

snapshots.name: Joab
snapshots.subtitle: David’s army commander
snapshots.body: Joab commands David’s army through decades of war, fiercely loyal yet willing to defy the king, as when he kills Absalom against direct orders. His ruthlessness catches up with him after David’s death.

snapshots.name: Solomon
snapshots.subtitle: King famed for wisdom
snapshots.body: Solomon succeeds his father David and asks God for wisdom rather than wealth, becoming famous for his judgments, his proverbs, and the Temple he builds in Jerusalem. His later years are marked by foreign alliances and idolatry that set the stage for the kingdom’s division.

snapshots.name: Rehoboam
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Solomon
snapshots.body: Rehoboam, Solomon’s son, answers the tribes’ request for lighter labor with threats of harsher rule, driving ten tribes to break away under Jeroboam and splitting the kingdom in two.

snapshots.name: Jeroboam
snapshots.subtitle: First king of the northern kingdom
snapshots.body: Jeroboam leads the ten northern tribes in breaking from Rehoboam and, fearing they will return their allegiance to Jerusalem, sets up golden calves for worship at Bethel and Dan, an act the text treats as the root sin of the northern kingdom.

snapshots.name: Elijah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of fire
snapshots.body: Elijah confronts King Ahab and the prophets of Baal, calling down fire from heaven on Mount Carmel to prove the LORD is God, yet flees in despair from Queen Jezebel afterward. He is finally taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, leaving his mantle to Elisha.

snapshots.name: Elisha
snapshots.subtitle: Successor to Elijah
snapshots.body: Elisha receives a double portion of Elijah’s spirit and performs a long string of miracles, from multiplying oil and raising a boy from death to healing the leprosy of the Aramean commander Naaman.

snapshots.name: Ahab
snapshots.subtitle: King of Israel married to Jezebel
snapshots.body: Ahab, king of the northern kingdom, marries the Phoenician princess Jezebel and promotes the worship of Baal, repeatedly clashing with Elijah. He dies in battle against Aram after ignoring a prophet’s warning.

snapshots.name: Jezebel
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Ahab
snapshots.body: Jezebel, a Phoenician princess who becomes Ahab’s queen, promotes Baal worship and has Naboth killed to seize his vineyard for her husband. She is thrown from a window and dies at Jehu’s command, her name becoming a byword for shameless wickedness.

snapshots.name: Naaman
snapshots.subtitle: Aramean army commander
snapshots.body: Naaman, a valiant Aramean commander afflicted with leprosy, is healed after a captive Israelite girl points him to Elisha, though he balks at first when told simply to wash in the Jordan seven times.

snapshots.name: Hezekiah
snapshots.subtitle: Reforming king of Judah
snapshots.body: Hezekiah removes idolatrous shrines and restores worship in Judah, and when the Assyrian king Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem, he prays in the Temple and sees the siege broken overnight. Later healed of a fatal illness, he unwisely shows off his treasures to Babylonian envoys.

snapshots.name: Sennacherib
snapshots.subtitle: King of Assyria
snapshots.body: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, conquers the fortified cities of Judah and besieges Jerusalem itself, sending a taunting message to Hezekiah before his army is struck down and he withdraws. He is later assassinated by his own sons.

snapshots.name: Josiah
snapshots.subtitle: Named in a prophecy
snapshots.body: A man of God foretells at Jeroboam’s altar at Bethel that a child named Josiah will one day be born to the house of David and will sacrifice on that altar the priests of the high places.

snapshots.name: Josiah
snapshots.subtitle: Reforming king of Judah
snapshots.body: Josiah becomes king as a child and, after a lost book of the law is rediscovered during Temple repairs, launches Judah’s most thorough religious reform, destroying idolatrous shrines throughout the land. He dies young in battle against Egypt at Megiddo.

snapshots.name: Nebuchadnezzar
snapshots.subtitle: King of Babylon
snapshots.body: Nebuchadnezzar conquers Jerusalem, destroys the Temple, and carries Judah’s people into exile in Babylon. In Daniel he is humbled by a period of madness for his pride before acknowledging the God of the exiles.

snapshots.name: Cyrus
snapshots.subtitle: Persian king who ends the exile
snapshots.body: Cyrus, the Persian king who conquers Babylon, issues the decree that allows the exiled Jews to return home and rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem, and is even called God’s anointed by Isaiah.

snapshots.name: Ezra
snapshots.subtitle: Priest and scribe of the return
snapshots.body: Ezra, a priest and scribe skilled in the law of Moses, leads a group of exiles back to Jerusalem and confronts the community over intermarriage with surrounding peoples, leading a public reading and renewal of the law.

snapshots.name: Nehemiah
snapshots.subtitle: Cupbearer who rebuilds Jerusalem’s walls
snapshots.body: Nehemiah, cupbearer to the Persian king, is granted leave to return to Jerusalem and organizes the rebuilding of its broken walls in the face of local opposition and sabotage. He also enforces reforms in worship and social justice among the returned exiles.

snapshots.name: Esther
snapshots.subtitle: Jewish queen of Persia
snapshots.body: Esther, a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, becomes queen of Persia and risks her life by appearing before the king unsummoned to expose a plot to destroy her people. Her courage turns the tables on Haman and saves the Jews of the empire.

snapshots.name: Mordecai
snapshots.subtitle: Esther’s cousin and guardian
snapshots.body: Mordecai, who raised his orphaned cousin Esther as his own daughter, refuses to bow to the king’s favorite Haman and uncovers a plot to destroy the Jews, urging Esther to intercede with the king.

snapshots.name: Haman
snapshots.subtitle: Persian official who plots against the Jews
snapshots.body: Haman, enraged that Mordecai will not bow to him, persuades the king to authorize the destruction of all Jews in the empire, then is hanged on the very gallows he built for Mordecai.

snapshots.name: Job
snapshots.subtitle: Righteous sufferer
snapshots.body: Job, a blameless and prosperous man, loses his children, wealth, and health in a series of disasters permitted by God to test his faith, and spends most of the book arguing with friends over why he suffers. God finally answers him out of a whirlwind, and Job’s fortunes are restored.

snapshots.name: Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar
snapshots.subtitle: Job’s three friends
snapshots.body: Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar sit with Job in his suffering and, across long speeches, insist his misfortune must be punishment for hidden sin. God later rebukes them for not speaking rightly about him, as Job had.

snapshots.name: Isaiah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of Judah
snapshots.body: Isaiah prophesies in Jerusalem across the reigns of several kings, warning of judgment on Judah’s injustice while also promising a future deliverer and a restored Zion. His book’s language of a suffering servant becomes central to later Christian reading of the Messiah.

snapshots.name: Jeremiah
snapshots.subtitle: Weeping prophet
snapshots.body: Jeremiah is called as a young man to prophesy Jerusalem’s coming destruction, a message that earns him persecution and imprisonment from his own people. He witnesses the city’s fall to Babylon and laments it, while also promising a future new covenant.

snapshots.name: Baruch
snapshots.subtitle: Jeremiah’s scribe
snapshots.body: Baruch is Jeremiah’s trusted scribe, who writes down the prophet’s words at his dictation and reads them aloud in the Temple, provoking the king’s anger. He stays with Jeremiah through imprisonment and eventual exile to Egypt.

snapshots.name: Ezekiel
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet among the exiles
snapshots.body: Ezekiel, a priest carried into exile in Babylon, receives strange visions of God’s glory and acts out prophetic signs against Jerusalem’s coming fall. After the city falls he turns to visions of restoration, including a valley of dry bones brought back to life.

snapshots.name: Daniel
snapshots.subtitle: Exile who interprets dreams
snapshots.body: Daniel, taken to Babylon as a young exile, rises to prominence by interpreting the dreams of Babylonian and Persian kings while keeping faithful to his own God. He survives a night in a den of lions and receives apocalyptic visions of future kingdoms.

snapshots.name: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
snapshots.subtitle: Daniel’s three companions
snapshots.body: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, exiled with Daniel, refuse to bow to Nebuchadnezzar’s golden image and are thrown into a furnace, from which they emerge unharmed alongside a fourth figure the king describes as like a son of the gods.

snapshots.name: Hosea
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of a broken marriage
snapshots.body: Hosea is told by God to marry a promiscuous woman as a living picture of Israel’s unfaithfulness, and his repeated forgiveness of her mirrors the persistence of God’s love for a wayward people.

snapshots.name: Amos
snapshots.subtitle: Shepherd prophet
snapshots.body: Amos, a shepherd from Judah with no prophetic pedigree, is sent north to condemn the wealthy northern kingdom for its exploitation of the poor beneath a veneer of religious observance.

snapshots.name: Jonah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet from Gath-hepher
snapshots.body: The prophet Jonah, son of Amittai, of Gath-hepher, is named as the servant of the LORD who foretold that Israel’s border would be restored.

snapshots.name: Jonah
snapshots.subtitle: Reluctant prophet
snapshots.body: Jonah flees by ship rather than preach repentance to Israel’s enemy Nineveh, is swallowed by a great fish after being thrown overboard, and finally delivers the message he resents when the city actually repents.

snapshots.name: Micah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of Moresheth
snapshots.body: Micah of Moresheth is remembered by the elders as the prophet who told King Hezekiah’s Judah that Zion would be plowed like a field.

snapshots.name: Micah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of Judah
snapshots.body: Micah prophesies alongside Isaiah against the corruption of both Israel and Judah, and is remembered for reducing true religion to a single line: to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.

snapshots.name: Malachi
snapshots.subtitle: Final prophet of the Old Testament
snapshots.body: Malachi confronts a returned but complacent post-exilic community over careless worship and broken faith, and closes the Old Testament looking forward to a messenger who will prepare the way before the LORD.

snapshots.name: Joel
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of the locust plague
snapshots.body: Joel takes a devastating locust plague as a sign of the coming day of the LORD, calling the people to fasting and repentance, and promises a future outpouring of God’s spirit on all people.

snapshots.name: Obadiah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet against Edom
snapshots.body: Obadiah delivers the shortest book in the Old Testament, a single oracle condemning Edom for gloating over Judah’s downfall and preying on its refugees.

snapshots.name: Nahum
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet against Nineveh
snapshots.body: Nahum prophesies the violent downfall of Nineveh, capital of the Assyrian empire that had once repented at Jonah’s preaching but returned to its cruelty.

snapshots.name: Habakkuk
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet who questions God
snapshots.body: Habakkuk openly questions why God tolerates injustice and permits Babylon to punish Judah, and is answered that the just will live by faith while ending his book in a hymn of trust regardless of circumstance.

snapshots.name: Zephaniah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of the day of the LORD
snapshots.body: Zephaniah, described as a descendant of King Hezekiah, warns Judah of a sweeping coming judgment while also promising a faithful remnant that God will rejoice over with singing.

snapshots.name: Zechariah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet in Jerusalem
snapshots.body: The prophet Zechariah, son of Iddo, prophesies with Haggai to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel.

snapshots.name: Zechariah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of the restoration
snapshots.body: Zechariah encourages the returned exiles to finish rebuilding the Temple through a series of visions, and his oracles about a coming king riding on a donkey and a pierced figure are later read as pointing to Jesus.

snapshots.name: Haggai
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet in Jerusalem
snapshots.body: The prophet Haggai prophesies with Zechariah to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel.

snapshots.name: Haggai
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet who spurs the Temple’s rebuilding
snapshots.body: Haggai rebukes the returned exiles for finishing their own houses while the LORD’s Temple lies in ruins, and his short, urgent oracles help spur the Temple’s reconstruction under Zerubbabel.

snapshots.name: Zerubbabel
snapshots.subtitle: Governor who rebuilds the Temple
snapshots.body: Zerubbabel, a descendant of David, leads the first group of exiles back from Babylon and oversees the rebuilding of the Temple, encouraged on by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah.

snapshots.name: Rahab
snapshots.subtitle: Woman of Jericho who hides the spies
snapshots.body: Rahab, a woman of Jericho, hides two Israelite spies on her roof and helps them escape in exchange for her family’s safety when the city falls, and is later remembered in the New Testament as an ancestor of David and an example of faith.

snapshots.name: Jehu
snapshots.subtitle: King who destroys the house of Ahab
snapshots.body: Jehu is anointed king and commissioned to wipe out the house of Ahab, killing Jezebel and the surviving royal line in a violent purge of Baal worship from Israel.

snapshots.name: Manasseh
snapshots.subtitle: Judah’s longest-reigning and most idolatrous king
snapshots.body: Manasseh reverses his father Hezekiah’s reforms, filling Jerusalem with idols and even sacrificing his own son, before being carried captive to Babylon, where he repents and is restored to his throne.

snapshots.name: Asa
snapshots.subtitle: Reforming king of Judah
snapshots.body: Asa removes idols and even his own grandmother from power for her idolatry, and relies on God for victory against a vastly larger invading army, though he later turns to foreign alliances instead.

snapshots.name: Jehoshaphat
snapshots.subtitle: Ally of the northern kings
snapshots.body: Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah and sends teachers throughout the land to instruct the people in the law, but is criticized for allying himself by marriage with the wicked house of Ahab.

snapshots.name: Bartholomew, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon the Zealot
snapshots.subtitle: The remaining apostles
snapshots.body: Alongside the more prominent disciples, the twelve include James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus (also called Judas the son of James), and Simon called the Zealot, each named in the Gospel lists of the twelve but given no individual story of their own.

snapshots.name: Jesus
snapshots.subtitle: Central figure of the New Testament
snapshots.body: Jesus of Nazareth is born to Mary and Joseph, baptized by John, and spends a public ministry of several years teaching, healing, and gathering disciples across Galilee and Judea. Crucified under Pontius Pilate at the urging of the religious authorities, he is proclaimed by his followers to have risen from the dead.

snapshots.name: Mary
snapshots.subtitle: Mother of Jesus
snapshots.body: Mary, a young woman of Nazareth, is told by an angel that she will conceive and bear a son who will be called the Son of the Most High, and later stands at the foot of the cross as he dies.

snapshots.name: Joseph
snapshots.subtitle: Husband of Mary
snapshots.body: Joseph, a carpenter betrothed to Mary, resolves to divorce her quietly on learning of her pregnancy until an angel explains it to him in a dream. He protects the family by fleeing to Egypt and raises Jesus as his own son.

snapshots.name: John the Baptist
snapshots.subtitle: Forerunner of Jesus
snapshots.body: John the Baptist preaches repentance in the wilderness of Judea, baptizing crowds in the Jordan and identifying Jesus as the one who was to come. His public condemnation of Herod Antipas’s marriage leads to his imprisonment and beheading.

snapshots.name: Simon Peter
snapshots.subtitle: Leading apostle
snapshots.body: Simon, a fisherman renamed Peter by Jesus and made the rock on which he says he will build his church, is the most prominent of the twelve apostles and the first to confess Jesus as the Christ. He denies knowing Jesus three times during the trial, then becomes a leading voice of the early church after the resurrection.

snapshots.name: Andrew
snapshots.subtitle: Apostle, brother of Peter
snapshots.body: Andrew, Peter’s brother and originally a follower of John the Baptist, is among the first to be called by Jesus and brings his brother to meet him.

snapshots.name: James son of Zebedee
snapshots.subtitle: Apostle, brother of John
snapshots.body: James, son of Zebedee and brother of John, is one of the inner circle of three apostles closest to Jesus, present at the transfiguration. He becomes the first apostle martyred, executed by Herod Agrippa I.

snapshots.name: John
snapshots.subtitle: Fisherman called by Jesus
snapshots.body: John, son of Zebedee and brother of James, is mending nets in a boat with his father when Jesus calls the two brothers, and they leave the boat and follow him.

snapshots.name: John
snapshots.subtitle: Apostle, the "beloved disciple"
snapshots.body: John, son of Zebedee and brother of James, is part of Jesus’s inner circle and is traditionally identified as the disciple Jesus loved, who reclines beside him at the last supper and receives care of Mary at the cross. He becomes a pillar of the Jerusalem church and, by tradition, the seer of the book of Revelation.

snapshots.name: Philip
snapshots.subtitle: Apostle from Bethsaida
snapshots.body: Philip, called early among the twelve, brings his friend Nathanael to Jesus and later asks Jesus at the last supper to show the disciples the Father.

snapshots.name: Nathanael
snapshots.subtitle: Apostle also called Bartholomew
snapshots.body: Nathanael is skeptical that anything good can come from Nazareth until he meets Jesus, who astonishes him by describing him sitting under a fig tree before they ever met. He is traditionally identified with the apostle Bartholomew.

snapshots.name: Thomas
snapshots.subtitle: Apostle called Didymus
snapshots.body: Thomas, called the Twin, is absent when the risen Jesus first appears to the other disciples and refuses to believe without touching his wounds himself. A week later Jesus lets him do exactly that, and Thomas responds with one of the Gospel’s clearest confessions of faith.

snapshots.name: Matthew
snapshots.subtitle: Tax collector called by Jesus
snapshots.body: Matthew, a tax collector also called Levi, is called from his tax booth to follow Jesus and hosts a dinner for him with other social outcasts, drawing criticism from religious leaders.

snapshots.name: Judas Iscariot
snapshots.subtitle: Apostle who betrays Jesus
snapshots.body: Judas Iscariot, keeper of the disciples’ money, agrees to betray Jesus to the religious authorities for thirty pieces of silver and identifies him with a kiss in Gethsemane. Overcome with remorse, he returns the money and hangs himself.

snapshots.name: Mary Magdalene
snapshots.subtitle: Follower of Jesus
snapshots.body: Mary Magdalene, healed by Jesus of seven demons, follows him and supports his ministry, remains at the cross when most male disciples flee, and is the first to see him risen and to report it to the others.

snapshots.name: Martha
snapshots.subtitle: Sister of Mary and Lazarus
snapshots.body: Martha, of the household at Bethany, is anxious over serving while her sister Mary sits listening to Jesus, and later confesses her faith in the resurrection when her brother Lazarus dies.

snapshots.name: Mary of Bethany
snapshots.subtitle: Sister of Martha and Lazarus
snapshots.body: Mary of Bethany sits at Jesus’s feet listening rather than helping with the housework, and later anoints his feet with costly perfume shortly before his death.

snapshots.name: Lazarus
snapshots.subtitle: Brother of Martha and Mary
snapshots.body: Lazarus of Bethany falls sick and dies while Jesus delays coming, and after four days in the tomb is raised back to life at Jesus’s command, an act that hardens the authorities’ resolve against Jesus.

snapshots.name: Nicodemus
snapshots.subtitle: Pharisee who visits Jesus by night
snapshots.body: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and member of the ruling council, comes to Jesus by night with questions and is told he must be born again. He later helps prepare Jesus’s body for burial.

snapshots.name: Zacchaeus
snapshots.subtitle: Tax collector of Jericho
snapshots.body: Zacchaeus, a wealthy chief tax collector too short to see over the crowd, climbs a tree to glimpse Jesus passing through Jericho and is rewarded when Jesus invites himself to his house.

snapshots.name: Pontius Pilate
snapshots.subtitle: Roman governor of Judea
snapshots.body: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor, finds no basis for a charge against Jesus but yields to the crowd’s demand for crucifixion, washing his hands of the decision. He later authorizes a guard for the tomb and, in Acts, is remembered as party to the plot against Jesus.

snapshots.name: Herod
snapshots.subtitle: King of Judea at Jesus’s birth
snapshots.body: Herod the Great, alarmed by the magi’s report of a newborn king, orders the killing of infant boys in Bethlehem in an attempt to eliminate a rival, though Jesus’s family escapes to Egypt.

snapshots.name: Herod Antipas
snapshots.subtitle: Tetrarch of Galilee
snapshots.body: Herod Antipas imprisons and beheads John the Baptist at his stepdaughter’s request, and later has Jesus brought before him during the trial, mocking him before sending him back to Pilate.

snapshots.name: Caiaphas
snapshots.subtitle: High priest who presides over Jesus’s trial
snapshots.body: Caiaphas, the high priest, presides over the council that condemns Jesus, arguing it is better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to be endangered.

snapshots.name: Barabbas
snapshots.subtitle: Prisoner released instead of Jesus
snapshots.body: Barabbas, a prisoner held for insurrection and murder, is released by Pilate at the crowd’s demand as part of a Passover custom, while Jesus is sent to be crucified in his place.

snapshots.name: Joseph of Arimathea
snapshots.subtitle: Secret disciple who buries Jesus
snapshots.body: Joseph of Arimathea, a wealthy council member and secret follower of Jesus, asks Pilate for the body after the crucifixion and lays it in his own new tomb.

snapshots.name: Stephen
snapshots.subtitle: First Christian martyr
snapshots.body: Stephen, one of seven men chosen to serve the early Jerusalem church, delivers a bold speech before the council tracing Israel’s history and is stoned to death, becoming Christianity’s first martyr while a young Saul looks on approvingly.

snapshots.name: Saul
snapshots.subtitle: Persecutor of the church
snapshots.body: Saul of Tarsus, a zealous Pharisee, actively persecutes the early church and consents to Stephen’s stoning, then sets out for Damascus with letters authorizing further arrests.

snapshots.name: Paul
snapshots.subtitle: Apostle to the Gentiles
snapshots.body: Blinded by a vision of the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus, Saul is transformed into Paul, the church’s most tireless missionary, planting congregations across Asia Minor and Greece on three long journeys. His letters to those churches make up much of the New Testament, and he is eventually taken to Rome as a prisoner.

snapshots.name: Barnabas
snapshots.subtitle: Missionary companion of Paul
snapshots.body: Barnabas, a Levite whose name means "son of encouragement," vouches for the newly converted Saul to a wary Jerusalem church and later travels with him on missionary journeys before the two part ways over a dispute.

snapshots.name: Ananias
snapshots.subtitle: Disciple who restores Paul’s sight
snapshots.body: Ananias, a disciple in Damascus, is sent by God to lay hands on the blinded Saul, restoring his sight and baptizing the man he had every reason to fear.

snapshots.name: Ananias and Sapphira
snapshots.subtitle: Couple struck dead for deceit
snapshots.body: Ananias and Sapphira, members of the early Jerusalem church, sell a property but secretly keep back part of the proceeds while claiming to give it all, and each falls dead on being confronted with the lie.

snapshots.name: Cornelius
snapshots.subtitle: Roman centurion
snapshots.body: Cornelius, a devout Roman centurion, is directed by a vision to send for Peter, whose own vision then convinces him that the gospel is not for Jews alone, opening the church to Gentiles.

snapshots.name: Lydia
snapshots.subtitle: Seller of purple in Philippi
snapshots.body: Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from Thyatira, is the first convert Paul records in Europe, and offers her home in Philippi as a base for the new congregation there.

snapshots.name: Silas
snapshots.subtitle: Missionary companion of Paul
snapshots.body: Silas travels with Paul on his second missionary journey and is imprisoned with him in Philippi, where the two sing hymns at midnight before an earthquake frees them.

snapshots.name: Timothy
snapshots.subtitle: Disciple at Lystra
snapshots.body: Timothy is a disciple at Lystra, the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father, well spoken of by the brothers there, whom Paul wants to take along on his journey.

snapshots.name: Timothy
snapshots.subtitle: Young companion of Paul
snapshots.body: Timothy, a young disciple of mixed Jewish and Greek parentage, becomes one of Paul’s closest companions and is entrusted with leading the church at Ephesus, receiving two of Paul’s most personal letters.

snapshots.name: Titus
snapshots.subtitle: Companion of Paul in Crete
snapshots.body: Titus, a Gentile convert and companion of Paul, is left to organize the church in Crete and receives a letter from Paul instructing him on appointing elders and sound teaching.

snapshots.name: Apollos
snapshots.subtitle: Eloquent teacher
snapshots.body: Apollos, an eloquent Alexandrian Jew well versed in the scriptures, is instructed more accurately in the faith by Priscilla and Aquila and becomes an effective, if divisive, teacher in Corinth.

snapshots.name: Priscilla and Aquila
snapshots.subtitle: Missionary couple
snapshots.body: Priscilla and Aquila, a husband and wife tentmaking team, host Paul in Corinth, instruct Apollos more fully in the faith, and appear repeatedly as hosts of house churches across the empire.

snapshots.name: Felix
snapshots.subtitle: Roman governor who imprisons Paul
snapshots.body: Felix, the Roman governor of Judea, hears Paul’s case repeatedly and keeps him in custody for two years, hoping for a bribe, without ever ruling on the charges.

snapshots.name: Festus
snapshots.subtitle: Roman governor who hears Paul’s appeal
snapshots.body: Festus, who succeeds Felix as governor, reviews Paul’s case with King Agrippa and, when Paul appeals to Caesar as a Roman citizen, sends him on to Rome.

snapshots.name: Agrippa
snapshots.subtitle: Jewish king who hears Paul
snapshots.body: King Agrippa, invited by Festus to hear Paul’s defense, is famously told by Paul that he is almost persuaded to become a Christian.

snapshots.name: Onesimus
snapshots.subtitle: Runaway slave
snapshots.body: Onesimus, a runaway slave who meets Paul in prison and becomes a believer, is sent back to his master Philemon carrying Paul’s letter urging that he be received as a brother.

snapshots.name: Philemon
snapshots.subtitle: Slave owner addressed by Paul’s letter
snapshots.body: Philemon, a wealthy Christian and host of a house church, receives Paul’s short personal letter asking him to forgive and welcome back his runaway slave Onesimus as a brother in the faith.

snapshots.name: James
snapshots.subtitle: Named among Jesus’s brothers
snapshots.body: James is named, with Joses, Simon and Judas, among the brothers of Jesus in Nazareth.

snapshots.name: James
snapshots.subtitle: Brother of Jesus, leader in Jerusalem
snapshots.body: James, described elsewhere as the Lord’s brother, becomes the leading figure of the Jerusalem church and presides over the council that decides Gentile converts need not follow the full Jewish law. The letter bearing his name stresses that faith without works is dead.

snapshots.name: Judas
snapshots.subtitle: Named among Jesus’s brothers
snapshots.body: Judas is named, with James, Joses and Simon, among the brothers of Jesus in Nazareth.

snapshots.name: Jude
snapshots.subtitle: Brother of Jesus and James
snapshots.body: Jude, brother of James and, by implication, of Jesus himself, writes a short, urgent letter warning churches against false teachers who twist grace into license.

snapshots.name: Mark
snapshots.subtitle: Gospel writer, companion of Paul and Peter
snapshots.body: John Mark accompanies Paul and Barnabas on a missionary journey but turns back partway, causing a rift between them, and later reconciles with Paul while also assisting Peter, traditionally the source behind his Gospel.

snapshots.name: Luke
snapshots.subtitle: Physician, author of Luke and Acts
snapshots.body: Luke, a physician and companion of Paul on parts of his travels, is traditionally credited as the author of the Gospel of Luke and the book of Acts, both addressed to a patron named Theophilus.

snapshots.name: Demetrius
snapshots.subtitle: Silversmith who riots against Paul
snapshots.body: Demetrius, a silversmith whose trade making shrines of the goddess Diana is threatened by Paul’s preaching, stirs up a riot in Ephesus in defense of his livelihood and his goddess.

snapshots.name: Simon Magus
snapshots.subtitle: Sorcerer who tries to buy the Spirit
snapshots.body: Simon Magus, a sorcerer who had amazed the people of Samaria, is baptized among the believers but is rebuked by Peter for offering money to buy the power of laying on hands.

snapshots.name: Caesar Augustus
snapshots.subtitle: Roman emperor at Jesus’s birth
snapshots.body: Caesar Augustus’s decree that a census be taken of the Roman world is the occasion that brings Joseph and the pregnant Mary to Bethlehem, where Jesus is born.

snapshots.name: Gamaliel
snapshots.subtitle: Respected Pharisee and teacher
snapshots.body: Gamaliel, a respected teacher of the law and, by tradition, Paul’s own teacher, advises the council to leave the apostles alone, reasoning that a merely human movement will collapse on its own.

snapshots.name: God
snapshots.subtitle: The LORD
snapshots.body: God is the central actor of the whole book: creator of heaven and earth, the covenant-making LORD of Israel who calls Abraham, delivers Israel from Egypt, and speaks through the prophets, and, in the New Testament, the Father whom Jesus reveals and to whom he prays.

snapshots.name: the Holy Spirit
snapshots.subtitle: Spirit of God
snapshots.body: The Holy Spirit hovers over the waters at creation, empowers judges and prophets, descends on Jesus at his baptism, and is poured out on the gathered disciples at Pentecost, filling the early church with power to preach and heal.

snapshots.name: Satan
snapshots.subtitle: The Adversary
snapshots.body: Satan appears as the serpent who tempts Eve, the accuser who tests Job with God’s permission, and the tempter who confronts Jesus in the wilderness, and reappears in Revelation as the dragon finally defeated.

snapshots.name: the serpent
snapshots.subtitle: Tempter in the garden
snapshots.body: The serpent, "more subtil than any beast of the field," persuades Eve to eat the forbidden fruit by questioning God’s word and promising that she will become like God, knowing good and evil.

snapshots.name: the Ark of the Covenant
snapshots.subtitle: Sacred chest of the Law
snapshots.body: The Ark of the Covenant, a gold-covered chest holding the tablets of the law, travels at the head of Israel through the wilderness and the conquest of Canaan, and is later captured and returned by the Philistines before coming to rest in Solomon’s Temple.

snapshots.name: the Temple
snapshots.subtitle: House of the LORD in Jerusalem
snapshots.body: The Temple, built by Solomon as a permanent house for the ark and for worship, is destroyed by the Babylonians, rebuilt modestly after the exile, and later expanded by Herod into the building Jesus visits, teaches in, and predicts will fall.

snapshots.name: Babylon
snapshots.subtitle: Empire and image of worldly power
snapshots.body: Babylon is both the historical empire that destroys Jerusalem and carries Judah into exile, and, especially in Revelation, a symbol of a proud, corrupt world power destined for sudden collapse.

snapshots.name: Zion
snapshots.subtitle: Jerusalem as God’s dwelling
snapshots.body: Zion, originally the hill David captures to found his city, becomes shorthand throughout the prophets and psalms for Jerusalem as the place of God’s presence and the hoped-for center of a restored world.

snapshots.name: the Word
snapshots.subtitle: Logos of John’s Gospel
snapshots.body: The Word, present with God from the beginning and identified as God, becomes flesh in John’s Gospel to dwell among humanity, full of grace and truth, in the person of Jesus.

snapshots.name: the Lamb
snapshots.subtitle: Image of Christ in Revelation
snapshots.body: The Lamb, described as looking as if it had been slain yet standing alive, is the central image of worship in Revelation’s heavenly throne room, the only one found worthy to open the sealed scroll of history.

snapshots.name: Adam
snapshots.subtitle: The first man
snapshots.body: Adam is formed from the dust and placed in the garden of Eden, given the task of naming the animals and tending the ground. His disobedience over the forbidden fruit brings him and his descendants out from Eden into a life of labor.

snapshots.name: Eve
snapshots.subtitle: The first woman
snapshots.body: Eve is formed from Adam’s side to be his companion and is deceived by the serpent into eating the forbidden fruit, which she shares with Adam. She becomes, in the text’s own words, "the mother of all living."

snapshots.name: Cain
snapshots.subtitle: Firstborn of Adam and Eve
snapshots.body: Cain is a tiller of the ground whose offering God rejects in favor of his brother Abel’s; consumed by jealousy, he murders Abel in the field. Marked by God and driven out, he becomes a wanderer and founds a city.

snapshots.name: Abel
snapshots.subtitle: Second son of Adam and Eve
snapshots.body: Abel is a keeper of sheep whose offering of the firstlings of his flock God accepts. He is murdered by his brother Cain, becoming the first death in the biblical narrative.

snapshots.name: Noah
snapshots.subtitle: Builder of the ark
snapshots.body: Noah is the one righteous man of his generation, instructed by God to build an ark to save his family and pairs of every animal from a coming flood. After the waters recede he offers sacrifice and receives God’s covenant, marked by the rainbow.

snapshots.name: Abram
snapshots.subtitle: Called out of Ur
snapshots.body: Abram is called by God to leave his country for a land he will be shown, with the promise that he will become a great nation. He journeys through Canaan and Egypt with his wife Sarai and nephew Lot, his faith tested repeatedly along the way.

snapshots.name: Abraham
snapshots.subtitle: Father of many nations
snapshots.body: Renamed by God as the sign of an everlasting covenant, Abraham becomes the father of Isaac in his old age and, in the Bible’s starkest test of faith, is asked to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah before an angel stays his hand. He dies at a great age and is buried beside Sarah at Machpelah.

snapshots.name: Sarai
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Abram
snapshots.body: Sarai is Abram’s wife, barren into old age, who gives her servant Hagar to Abram so that he might have an heir through her instead.

snapshots.name: Sarah
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Abraham, mother of Isaac
snapshots.body: Renamed by God alongside her husband, Sarah laughs at the promise that she will bear a son in her old age, then names that son Isaac, meaning laughter, when he is born. She dies at Hebron and is the first person buried in the cave of Machpelah.

snapshots.name: Hagar
snapshots.subtitle: Egyptian servant of Sarah
snapshots.body: Hagar bears Abraham a son, Ishmael, and is twice driven into the wilderness, where an angel finds and comforts her. She becomes the mother of a great nation in her own right, through Ishmael.

snapshots.name: Ishmael
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Abraham and Hagar
snapshots.body: Ishmael is Abraham’s firstborn son, born of Hagar, sent away with his mother once Isaac is born but promised by God that he too will father a great nation. He grows up an archer in the wilderness of Paran.

snapshots.name: Isaac
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Abraham and Sarah
snapshots.body: Isaac is the long-promised son of Abraham’s old age, nearly offered as a sacrifice on Mount Moriah before God provides a ram instead. He marries Rebekah, and in his old age is deceived into giving his blessing to Jacob instead of Esau.

snapshots.name: Rebekah
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Isaac
snapshots.body: Rebekah is chosen at a well by Abraham’s servant to be Isaac’s wife, and later favors her younger son Jacob, helping him deceive the blind Isaac into giving him the blessing meant for Esau.

snapshots.name: Jacob
snapshots.subtitle: Younger son of Isaac and Rebekah
snapshots.body: Jacob buys his brother Esau’s birthright for a bowl of stew and later disguises himself to steal their father’s blessing, fleeing to his uncle Laban’s house. There he marries Leah and Rachel and grows wealthy in flocks before setting out for home.

snapshots.name: Israel
snapshots.subtitle: Father of the twelve tribes
snapshots.body: Renamed after wrestling all night with a divine stranger at Peniel, Jacob becomes Israel and is reconciled with Esau. His twelve sons by four women become the twelve tribes, and in his old age he is reunited with his son Joseph in Egypt.

snapshots.name: Esau
snapshots.subtitle: Elder son of Isaac and Rebekah, twin of Jacob
snapshots.body: Esau is a skillful hunter who sells his birthright to his brother Jacob for a meal and is later cheated of their father’s blessing as well. Years later he greets the returning Jacob with an embrace rather than the vengeance Jacob feared.

snapshots.name: Rachel
snapshots.subtitle: Younger wife of Jacob
snapshots.body: Rachel is Jacob’s beloved wife, for whom he labors fourteen years, and the long-barren mother of Joseph and Benjamin. She dies giving birth to Benjamin on the road to Bethlehem.

snapshots.name: Leah
snapshots.subtitle: Elder wife of Jacob
snapshots.body: Leah is given to Jacob in place of her sister Rachel through her father Laban’s deception, and bears him six sons including Judah and Levi, ancestors of the priestly and royal lines.

snapshots.name: Joseph
snapshots.subtitle: Favored son of Jacob
snapshots.body: Joseph, favored by his father and given a coat of many colors, is sold into slavery in Egypt by his jealous brothers. Through dream interpretation he rises to become Pharaoh’s chief minister and later saves his own family from famine, forgiving his brothers.

snapshots.name: Judah
snapshots.subtitle: Fourth son of Jacob and Leah
snapshots.body: Judah persuades his brothers to sell Joseph rather than kill him, and later offers himself as a slave in place of Benjamin, moving Joseph to reveal himself. His descendants become the royal tribe from which David and, in Christian reading, Jesus descend.

snapshots.name: Benjamin
snapshots.subtitle: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel
snapshots.body: Benjamin is Jacob’s youngest and most cherished son, born at the cost of his mother Rachel’s life. His brothers’ fear of losing him too becomes the turning point that leads Joseph to reveal himself to them in Egypt.

snapshots.name: Lot
snapshots.subtitle: Nephew of Abraham
snapshots.body: Lot travels with his uncle Abraham before settling near the wicked city of Sodom, from which he is rescued by angels just before its destruction. His wife looks back at the ruin and is turned to a pillar of salt.

snapshots.name: Melchizedek
snapshots.subtitle: Priest-king of Salem
snapshots.body: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blesses Abram and receives a tithe from him after a battle. Later writers use him as a type of an eternal priesthood outside the ordinary Levitical line.

snapshots.name: Moses
snapshots.subtitle: Deliverer and lawgiver
snapshots.body: Moses, drawn from the Nile as a baby and raised in Pharaoh’s household, flees to Midian after killing an Egyptian and is called by God from a burning bush to free the Israelites from slavery. He leads them through the parted sea, receives the law at Sinai, and guides them through forty years in the wilderness, though he himself dies before entering the promised land.

snapshots.name: Aaron
snapshots.subtitle: Brother of Moses, first high priest
snapshots.body: Aaron serves as Moses’s spokesman before Pharaoh and performs signs with his rod, but also casts the golden calf the people worship in Moses’s absence. He is later consecrated as Israel’s first high priest, a role that passes to his descendants.

snapshots.name: Miriam
snapshots.subtitle: Sister of Moses and Aaron
snapshots.body: Miriam watches over the infant Moses in the bulrushes and later leads the women of Israel in song after the crossing of the sea. She is struck with a skin disease after challenging Moses’s authority and dies in the wilderness at Kadesh.

snapshots.name: Pharaoh
snapshots.subtitle: King of Egypt at the exodus
snapshots.body: The Pharaoh of the exodus enslaves the Israelites and repeatedly refuses Moses’s demand to let them go, his heart hardening through ten devastating plagues. He pursues the departing Israelites to the Red Sea, where his army is destroyed.

snapshots.name: Joshua
snapshots.subtitle: Moses’s chosen fighter
snapshots.body: Joshua is the man Moses tells to choose men and go out to fight Amalek at Rephidim, while Moses stands on the hilltop with the rod of God in his hand.

snapshots.name: Joshua
snapshots.subtitle: Successor to Moses
snapshots.body: Joshua, one of the twelve spies sent into Canaan and one of only two who urged trust in God’s promise, succeeds Moses as leader of Israel. He leads the conquest of Canaan, beginning with the fall of Jericho, and divides the land among the tribes.

snapshots.name: Caleb
snapshots.subtitle: Spy of the tribe of Judah
snapshots.body: Caleb is the other of the twelve spies who, with Joshua, trusted God’s promise about Canaan against the fearful report of the majority. For his faith he is granted the hill country of Hebron as his inheritance in old age.

snapshots.name: Balaam
snapshots.subtitle: Hired prophet
snapshots.body: Balaam is a foreign prophet hired by King Balak to curse Israel, but is stopped on the road by an angel his donkey sees before he does. He ultimately can only bless Israel, though he later corrupts them by another scheme.

snapshots.name: Deborah
snapshots.subtitle: Judge and prophetess
snapshots.body: Deborah is a prophetess and judge who summons Barak to lead Israel’s army against the Canaanite general Sisera, and sings a victory song afterward. Her sure-footed leadership is contrasted with Barak’s hesitance.

snapshots.name: Gideon
snapshots.subtitle: Judge who defeats Midian
snapshots.body: Gideon, threshing wheat in hiding from Midianite raiders, is called by an angel to deliver Israel and tests God twice with a fleece before acting. With a force cut down to just three hundred men, he routs the Midianite camp by night with torches and trumpets.

snapshots.name: Samson
snapshots.subtitle: Nazirite strongman
snapshots.body: Samson, a judge of Israel set apart from birth and given great strength as long as his hair is uncut, wages a one-man war against the Philistines. Betrayed by Delilah, who learns the secret of his strength, he is blinded and enslaved before pulling down a temple on his captors in his final act.

snapshots.name: Delilah
snapshots.subtitle: Philistine woman who betrays Samson
snapshots.body: Delilah is bribed by the Philistine lords to discover the secret of Samson’s strength, and after repeated attempts wears him down until he tells her the truth about his hair. She has it cut while he sleeps, delivering him into his enemies’ hands.

snapshots.name: Ruth
snapshots.subtitle: Moabite widow
snapshots.body: Ruth, a Moabite widow, refuses to leave her mother-in-law Naomi and returns with her to Bethlehem, gleaning in the fields to support them both. Her loyalty leads to marriage with Boaz, and she becomes an ancestor of David.

snapshots.name: Naomi
snapshots.subtitle: Mother-in-law of Ruth
snapshots.body: Naomi, widowed and having lost both her sons in Moab, returns to Bethlehem bitter with grief, urging her daughters-in-law to remain behind. Ruth’s loyalty and the birth of a grandson restore her.

snapshots.name: Boaz
snapshots.subtitle: Kinsman-redeemer of Ruth
snapshots.body: Boaz, a wealthy relative of Naomi’s late husband, shows Ruth favor in his fields and, following custom, redeems her through marriage. Their son Obed becomes the grandfather of David.

snapshots.name: Samuel
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet and last judge
snapshots.body: Samuel, given to the LORD’s service by his mother Hannah before his birth, hears God’s voice as a boy in the temple at Shiloh and grows into Israel’s last judge and a prophet. He anoints first Saul and then David as king, and rebukes Saul when he disobeys God.

snapshots.name: Eli
snapshots.subtitle: Priest and judge at Shiloh
snapshots.body: Eli, the priest who raises the boy Samuel at the tabernacle in Shiloh, fails to restrain his own corrupt sons. He dies of shock on hearing that the ark of God has been captured in battle.

snapshots.name: Saul
snapshots.subtitle: First king of Israel
snapshots.body: Saul, a tall young Benjamite chosen and anointed as Israel’s first king, wins early victories but is rejected by God for repeated disobedience. Tormented by jealousy of David and an evil spirit, he ends his reign in defeat, taking his own life on Mount Gilboa.

snapshots.name: David
snapshots.subtitle: Descendant of Ruth and Boaz
snapshots.body: David is named at the end of the book of Ruth as the son of Jesse, whose line is traced back through Obed to Boaz and Ruth.

snapshots.name: David
snapshots.subtitle: Shepherd who becomes king
snapshots.body: David, the youngest son of Jesse anointed in secret by Samuel, kills the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and rises from court musician to fugitive to king. He unites Israel, captures Jerusalem, and is promised an everlasting dynasty, though his reign is marred by his affair with Bathsheba and family rebellion.

snapshots.name: Bathsheba
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Uriah, then of David
snapshots.body: Bathsheba is seen bathing by David, who sends for her and, on learning she is pregnant, arranges the death of her husband Uriah to cover the affair. The child of the affair dies, but she later bears Solomon and secures his succession to the throne.

snapshots.name: Uriah the Hittite
snapshots.subtitle: Bathsheba’s husband
snapshots.body: Uriah is a loyal soldier in David’s army whose refusal to visit his own house while his comrades are at war leads David to have him placed at the front of the fiercest fighting, where he is killed.

snapshots.name: Nathan
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet under David
snapshots.body: Nathan the prophet confronts David over Bathsheba and Uriah with a parable that exposes the king’s own guilt, and later ensures that Solomon rather than a rival son succeeds to the throne.

snapshots.name: Jonathan
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Saul, friend of David
snapshots.body: Jonathan, Saul’s son and heir, forms a deep friendship with David and repeatedly protects him from his father’s jealous rage, even though it costs him the throne. He dies alongside Saul in battle against the Philistines.

snapshots.name: Absalom
snapshots.subtitle: Son of David
snapshots.body: Absalom avenges his sister Tamar by killing their brother Amnon, then later leads an open rebellion against his father David. His revolt collapses and he dies caught by his hair in a tree, grieved deeply by David despite the betrayal.

snapshots.name: Joab
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Zeruiah
snapshots.body: Joab is named as the brother of Abishai and the son of Zeruiah, one of the men who follow David.

snapshots.name: Joab
snapshots.subtitle: David’s army commander
snapshots.body: Joab commands David’s army through decades of war, fiercely loyal yet willing to defy the king, as when he kills Absalom against direct orders. His ruthlessness catches up with him after David’s death.

snapshots.name: Solomon
snapshots.subtitle: King famed for wisdom
snapshots.body: Solomon succeeds his father David and asks God for wisdom rather than wealth, becoming famous for his judgments, his proverbs, and the Temple he builds in Jerusalem. His later years are marked by foreign alliances and idolatry that set the stage for the kingdom’s division.

snapshots.name: Rehoboam
snapshots.subtitle: Son of Solomon
snapshots.body: Rehoboam, Solomon’s son, answers the tribes’ request for lighter labor with threats of harsher rule, driving ten tribes to break away under Jeroboam and splitting the kingdom in two.

snapshots.name: Jeroboam
snapshots.subtitle: First king of the northern kingdom
snapshots.body: Jeroboam leads the ten northern tribes in breaking from Rehoboam and, fearing they will return their allegiance to Jerusalem, sets up golden calves for worship at Bethel and Dan, an act the text treats as the root sin of the northern kingdom.

snapshots.name: Elijah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of fire
snapshots.body: Elijah confronts King Ahab and the prophets of Baal, calling down fire from heaven on Mount Carmel to prove the LORD is God, yet flees in despair from Queen Jezebel afterward. He is finally taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, leaving his mantle to Elisha.

snapshots.name: Elisha
snapshots.subtitle: Successor to Elijah
snapshots.body: Elisha receives a double portion of Elijah’s spirit and performs a long string of miracles, from multiplying oil and raising a boy from death to healing the leprosy of the Aramean commander Naaman.

snapshots.name: Ahab
snapshots.subtitle: King of Israel married to Jezebel
snapshots.body: Ahab, king of the northern kingdom, marries the Phoenician princess Jezebel and promotes the worship of Baal, repeatedly clashing with Elijah. He dies in battle against Aram after ignoring a prophet’s warning.

snapshots.name: Jezebel
snapshots.subtitle: Wife of Ahab
snapshots.body: Jezebel, a Phoenician princess who becomes Ahab’s queen, promotes Baal worship and has Naboth killed to seize his vineyard for her husband. She is thrown from a window and dies at Jehu’s command, her name becoming a byword for shameless wickedness.

snapshots.name: Naaman
snapshots.subtitle: Aramean army commander
snapshots.body: Naaman, a valiant Aramean commander afflicted with leprosy, is healed after a captive Israelite girl points him to Elisha, though he balks at first when told simply to wash in the Jordan seven times.

snapshots.name: Hezekiah
snapshots.subtitle: Reforming king of Judah
snapshots.body: Hezekiah removes idolatrous shrines and restores worship in Judah, and when the Assyrian king Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem, he prays in the Temple and sees the siege broken overnight. Later healed of a fatal illness, he unwisely shows off his treasures to Babylonian envoys.

snapshots.name: Sennacherib
snapshots.subtitle: King of Assyria
snapshots.body: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, conquers the fortified cities of Judah and besieges Jerusalem itself, sending a taunting message to Hezekiah before his army is struck down and he withdraws. He is later assassinated by his own sons.

snapshots.name: Josiah
snapshots.subtitle: Named in a prophecy
snapshots.body: A man of God foretells at Jeroboam’s altar at Bethel that a child named Josiah will one day be born to the house of David and will sacrifice on that altar the priests of the high places.

snapshots.name: Josiah
snapshots.subtitle: Reforming king of Judah
snapshots.body: Josiah becomes king as a child and, after a lost book of the law is rediscovered during Temple repairs, launches Judah’s most thorough religious reform, destroying idolatrous shrines throughout the land. He dies young in battle against Egypt at Megiddo.

snapshots.name: Nebuchadnezzar
snapshots.subtitle: King of Babylon
snapshots.body: Nebuchadnezzar conquers Jerusalem, destroys the Temple, and carries Judah’s people into exile in Babylon. In Daniel he is humbled by a period of madness for his pride before acknowledging the God of the exiles.

snapshots.name: Cyrus
snapshots.subtitle: Persian king who ends the exile
snapshots.body: Cyrus, the Persian king who conquers Babylon, issues the decree that allows the exiled Jews to return home and rebuild the Temple in Jerusalem, and is even called God’s anointed by Isaiah.

snapshots.name: Ezra
snapshots.subtitle: Priest and scribe of the return
snapshots.body: Ezra, a priest and scribe skilled in the law of Moses, leads a group of exiles back to Jerusalem and confronts the community over intermarriage with surrounding peoples, leading a public reading and renewal of the law.

snapshots.name: Nehemiah
snapshots.subtitle: Cupbearer who rebuilds Jerusalem’s walls
snapshots.body: Nehemiah, cupbearer to the Persian king, is granted leave to return to Jerusalem and organizes the rebuilding of its broken walls in the face of local opposition and sabotage. He also enforces reforms in worship and social justice among the returned exiles.

snapshots.name: Esther
snapshots.subtitle: Jewish queen of Persia
snapshots.body: Esther, a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, becomes queen of Persia and risks her life by appearing before the king unsummoned to expose a plot to destroy her people. Her courage turns the tables on Haman and saves the Jews of the empire.

snapshots.name: Mordecai
snapshots.subtitle: Esther’s cousin and guardian
snapshots.body: Mordecai, who raised his orphaned cousin Esther as his own daughter, refuses to bow to the king’s favorite Haman and uncovers a plot to destroy the Jews, urging Esther to intercede with the king.

snapshots.name: Haman
snapshots.subtitle: Persian official who plots against the Jews
snapshots.body: Haman, enraged that Mordecai will not bow to him, persuades the king to authorize the destruction of all Jews in the empire, then is hanged on the very gallows he built for Mordecai.

snapshots.name: Job
snapshots.subtitle: Righteous sufferer
snapshots.body: Job, a blameless and prosperous man, loses his children, wealth, and health in a series of disasters permitted by God to test his faith, and spends most of the book arguing with friends over why he suffers. God finally answers him out of a whirlwind, and Job’s fortunes are restored.

snapshots.name: Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar
snapshots.subtitle: Job’s three friends
snapshots.body: Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar sit with Job in his suffering and, across long speeches, insist his misfortune must be punishment for hidden sin. God later rebukes them for not speaking rightly about him, as Job had.

snapshots.name: Isaiah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of Judah
snapshots.body: Isaiah prophesies in Jerusalem across the reigns of several kings, warning of judgment on Judah’s injustice while also promising a future deliverer and a restored Zion. His book’s language of a suffering servant becomes central to later Christian reading of the Messiah.

snapshots.name: Jeremiah
snapshots.subtitle: Weeping prophet
snapshots.body: Jeremiah is called as a young man to prophesy Jerusalem’s coming destruction, a message that earns him persecution and imprisonment from his own people. He witnesses the city’s fall to Babylon and laments it, while also promising a future new covenant.

snapshots.name: Baruch
snapshots.subtitle: Jeremiah’s scribe
snapshots.body: Baruch is Jeremiah’s trusted scribe, who writes down the prophet’s words at his dictation and reads them aloud in the Temple, provoking the king’s anger. He stays with Jeremiah through imprisonment and eventual exile to Egypt.

snapshots.name: Ezekiel
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet among the exiles
snapshots.body: Ezekiel, a priest carried into exile in Babylon, receives strange visions of God’s glory and acts out prophetic signs against Jerusalem’s coming fall. After the city falls he turns to visions of restoration, including a valley of dry bones brought back to life.

snapshots.name: Daniel
snapshots.subtitle: Exile who interprets dreams
snapshots.body: Daniel, taken to Babylon as a young exile, rises to prominence by interpreting the dreams of Babylonian and Persian kings while keeping faithful to his own God. He survives a night in a den of lions and receives apocalyptic visions of future kingdoms.

snapshots.name: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
snapshots.subtitle: Daniel’s three companions
snapshots.body: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, exiled with Daniel, refuse to bow to Nebuchadnezzar’s golden image and are thrown into a furnace, from which they emerge unharmed alongside a fourth figure the king describes as like a son of the gods.

snapshots.name: Hosea
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of a broken marriage
snapshots.body: Hosea is told by God to marry a promiscuous woman as a living picture of Israel’s unfaithfulness, and his repeated forgiveness of her mirrors the persistence of God’s love for a wayward people.

snapshots.name: Amos
snapshots.subtitle: Shepherd prophet
snapshots.body: Amos, a shepherd from Judah with no prophetic pedigree, is sent north to condemn the wealthy northern kingdom for its exploitation of the poor beneath a veneer of religious observance.

snapshots.name: Jonah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet from Gath-hepher
snapshots.body: The prophet Jonah, son of Amittai, of Gath-hepher, is named as the servant of the LORD who foretold that Israel’s border would be restored.

snapshots.name: Jonah
snapshots.subtitle: Reluctant prophet
snapshots.body: Jonah flees by ship rather than preach repentance to Israel’s enemy Nineveh, is swallowed by a great fish after being thrown overboard, and finally delivers the message he resents when the city actually repents.

snapshots.name: Micah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of Moresheth
snapshots.body: Micah of Moresheth is remembered by the elders as the prophet who told King Hezekiah’s Judah that Zion would be plowed like a field.

snapshots.name: Micah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of Judah
snapshots.body: Micah prophesies alongside Isaiah against the corruption of both Israel and Judah, and is remembered for reducing true religion to a single line: to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with God.

snapshots.name: Malachi
snapshots.subtitle: Final prophet of the Old Testament
snapshots.body: Malachi confronts a returned but complacent post-exilic community over careless worship and broken faith, and closes the Old Testament looking forward to a messenger who will prepare the way before the LORD.

snapshots.name: Joel
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of the locust plague
snapshots.body: Joel takes a devastating locust plague as a sign of the coming day of the LORD, calling the people to fasting and repentance, and promises a future outpouring of God’s spirit on all people.

snapshots.name: Obadiah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet against Edom
snapshots.body: Obadiah delivers the shortest book in the Old Testament, a single oracle condemning Edom for gloating over Judah’s downfall and preying on its refugees.

snapshots.name: Nahum
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet against Nineveh
snapshots.body: Nahum prophesies the violent downfall of Nineveh, capital of the Assyrian empire that had once repented at Jonah’s preaching but returned to its cruelty.

snapshots.name: Habakkuk
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet who questions God
snapshots.body: Habakkuk openly questions why God tolerates injustice and permits Babylon to punish Judah, and is answered that the just will live by faith while ending his book in a hymn of trust regardless of circumstance.

snapshots.name: Zephaniah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of the day of the LORD
snapshots.body: Zephaniah, described as a descendant of King Hezekiah, warns Judah of a sweeping coming judgment while also promising a faithful remnant that God will rejoice over with singing.

snapshots.name: Zechariah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet in Jerusalem
snapshots.body: The prophet Zechariah, son of Iddo, prophesies with Haggai to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel.

snapshots.name: Zechariah
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet of the restoration
snapshots.body: Zechariah encourages the returned exiles to finish rebuilding the Temple through a series of visions, and his oracles about a coming king riding on a donkey and a pierced figure are later read as pointing to Jesus.

snapshots.name: Haggai
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet in Jerusalem
snapshots.body: The prophet Haggai prophesies with Zechariah to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel.

snapshots.name: Haggai
snapshots.subtitle: Prophet who spurs the Temple’s rebuilding
snapshots.body: Haggai rebukes the returned exiles for finishing their own houses while the LORD’s Temple lies in ruins, and his short, urgent oracles help spur the Temple’s reconstruction under Zerubbabel.

snapshots.name: Zerubbabel
snapshots.subtitle: Governor who rebuilds the Temple
snapshots.body: Zerubbabel, a descendant of David, leads the first group of exiles back from Babylon and oversees the rebuilding of the Temple, encouraged on by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah.

snapshots.name: Rahab
snapshots.subtitle: Woman of Jericho who hides the spies
snapshots.body: Rahab, a woman of Jericho, hides two Israelite spies on her roof and helps them escape in exchange for her family’s safety when the city falls, and is later remembered in the New Testament as an ancestor of David and an example of faith.

snapshots.name: Jehu
snapshots.subtitle: King who destroys the house of Ahab
snapshots.body: Jehu is anointed king and commissioned to wipe out the house of Ahab, killing Jezebel and the surviving royal line in a violent purge of Baal worship from Israel.

snapshots.name: Manasseh
snapshots.subtitle: Judah’s longest-reigning and most idolatrous king
snapshots.body: Manasseh reverses his father Hezekiah’s reforms, filling Jerusalem with idols and even sacrificing his own son, before being carried captive to Babylon, where he repents and is restored to his throne.

snapshots.name: Asa
snapshots.subtitle: Reforming king of Judah
snapshots.body: Asa removes idols and even his own grandmother from power for her idolatry, and relies on God for victory against a vastly larger invading army, though he later turns to foreign alliances instead.

snapshots.name: Jehoshaphat
snapshots.subtitle: Ally of the northern kings
snapshots.body: Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah and sends teachers throughout the land to instruct the people in the law, but is criticized for allying himself by marriage with the wicked house of Ahab.

snapshots.name: Bartholomew, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon the Zealot
snapshots.subtitle: The remaining apostles
snapshots.body: Alongside the more prominent disciples, the twelve include James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus (also called Judas the son of James), and Simon called the Zealot, each named in the Gospel lists of the twelve but given no individual story of their own.

snapshots.name: Jesus
snapshots.subtitle: Central figure of the New Testament
snapshots.body: Jesus of Nazareth is born to Mary and Joseph, baptized by John, and spends a public ministry of several years teaching, healing, and gathering disciples across Galilee and Judea. Crucified under Pontius Pilate at the urging of the religious authorities, he is proclaimed by his followers to have risen from the dead.

snapshots.name: Mary
snapshots.subtitle: Mother of Jesus
snapshots.body: Mary, a young woman of Nazareth, is told by an angel that she will conceive and bear a son who will be called the Son of the Most High, and later stands at the foot of the cross as he dies.

snapshots.name: Joseph
snapshots.subtitle: Husband of Mary
